artboards.title: Overview — first week, nothing recorded yet
The headline in all three honest states

annotations.text:
SAME LANGUAGE AS THE CHANNEL WORKSPACE

This is not a card grid any more. It is the workspace's own report anatomy, chapter for chapter:

• Full-bleed verdict band, then the Potential / Lost / Earned scale — 224px box, 160px track, 2px bar tops, slate-200 base, emerald-500 for what is proven.

• A run-status strip stating exactly what is on screen.

• A flat chapter map, not a sticky tracker.

• Each chapter: an 8-column card (11px uppercase title at 0.18em, state chip) beside a 4-column rail carrying one big mono figure, one calm sentence, the emerald advice box, and one way into the evidence.

• The awaiting shelf and the dl footer close it, as they do there.

WHAT CAME FROM ELSEWHERE

Three moves borrowed from good product overviews (Stripe, Linear, Mercury) that the workspace does not have yet:

• A period comparison on the headline figure — +8.2% against the previous thirty days, with the prior figure named so it can be checked.

• A busiest-day callout pinned to the actual peak, so the chart answers a question rather than just existing.

• A last-updated stamp in the status strip.

Everything else is the app's own vocabulary. No new colours, no new radii, no new type sizes.

THE RANGE IS THE POINT

The old page said "indicative margin upper bound". A client heard nothing.

The headline now says: you kept AT LEAST X, and the truth is between X and Y. Same governance rule, said in money.

The dashed outline on the Kept bar is that ceiling drawn to scale, so the unproven part has a size.

Three states, bottom right.

WHAT WAS CUT

• Strategic Briefing — it restated the numbers below. Now it is the headline sentence and the rails.

• Integration Health card — a broken connection is chapter 01; a working one is a line in chapter 05.

• Digital Twin data dump and Organization Management — configuration is not an overview. Footer links.

• Campaign ideas from demo fixtures — now on the awaiting shelf, naming what each one waits on.
